one_liner: Administrative and mission-support analyst for ICE Health Service Corps' medical air, ground and maritime operations unit, filled only by commissioned U.S. Public Health Service officers.
fit_summary: The duties (travel, property, budget tracking, readiness coordination) overlap with Daniel's logistics and operations work at IEM, but only USPHS officers and Call to Active Duty candidates can apply, so he cannot apply as a civilian. Becoming a CAD candidate requires a degree that fits a USPHS officer category and a separate commissioning process.
eligibility: Open only to current U.S. Public Health Service commissioned officers and Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates, despite the 'public' hiring path label.
Requires a qualifying degree for a USPHS officer category plus three years of professional experience relevant to that category.
Requires at least three years of experience in management, administration or evaluation of programs.
Must maintain BLS for Healthcare Providers certification (American Heart Association).
Must be able to attain and maintain a DHS Secret clearance.
strategy: Don't spend time applying to this posting. Your civilian application would be screened out because it is USPHS/CAD-only.
If a USPHS commission interests him, check usphs.gov; an M.A. in Global Affairs likely doesn't fit an officer category, so this path is unlikely.

Use this posting as a keyword template for civilian mission-support jobs. Search USAJOBS for open-to-public GS-0343 Program Analyst and GS-0301 Mission Support roles at FEMA, ICE, CBP and DHS that use the same language.
Frame your IEM work around concrete readiness, logistics, deployment-support, data-tracking and reporting tasks for government clients. List hours per week and keep the resume within two pages.
Emphasize your relationship-building and stakeholder coordination, which fit the posting's interpersonal and cultural competencies.
Consider Virginia VDEM or Prince William County / City of Manassas emergency management positions as nearer-term civilian targets.
interview_questions: Describe a time you handled competing logistics demands when a mission or deployment changed suddenly.
How have you tracked expenditures or property and used the data to recommend cost-effective purchases?
Tell us about coordinating across multiple offices or stakeholders to meet a deadline.
How do you keep current with federal regulations and policies that affect your work?
watch_outs: Ineligible as a civilian: the posting is restricted to USPHS officers and CAD candidates.
Requires a USPHS-category degree and BLS for Healthcare Providers certification.
Requires a Secret clearance, may cancel leave for missions, and has no promotion potential.
